title: Antidepressant use late in pregnancy and risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
authors: Huybrechts KF, Bateman BT, Palmsten K, Desai RJ, Patorno E, Gopalakrishnan C, et al.
population: Pregnant women enrolled in US Medicaid, 2000 to 2010; 102,179 used an SSRI in the 90 days before delivery
funder: This study was supported by grant R01 HS018533 from the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality; individual career and training grants from NIMH and NICHD. The funders had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
result: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn in 20.8 per 10,000 births without antidepressant exposure and 31.5 per 10,000 after late-pregnancy SSRI exposure (322 infants). Odds ratio 1.51 (95% CI 1.35 to 1.69) unadjusted and 1.10 (0.94 to 1.29) when restricted to women with depression with high-dimensional propensity score adjustment; for primary PPHN, adjusted OR 1.28 (1.01 to 1.64).
